Glossary

ziran 自然

self-so; what is so of itself

Chinese (pinyin) · glossed in English

Glossary / ziran

A term is not a word. It is a working part of somebody's argument, and the English word usually offered for it is a compromise. This page gives the compromise, the argument, and the reading the sources do not support.

Where it is filed: Nature · Way · Simplicity · Freedom · Order · Being

What the term does

Ziran literally means 'so-of-itself' and was originally an adverbial pair, describing the way something is without an external cause rather than naming a domain of things. The Daodejing's statement that humans follow earth, earth follows heaven, heaven follows dao, and dao follows ziran is the pivot: it makes ziran the last term, which is why translating it as 'nature' with a definite article changes the argument. The modern Chinese and Japanese word for nature is this phrase, in a sense that arrived later.

The reading the sources do not support

Rendered as 'nature', which invites the reading that dao follows the natural world. The pre-modern sense is that dao follows no prescription at all — it is the condition of being so of itself. This is one of the terms where the modern meaning of the graph rather than its original sense is what most translations use.

Where it sits in the discipline

Metaphysics · Political philosophy · Philosophy of science

Terms that travel with it

  • dao — way, path, course
  • wu wei — non-coercive action; acting without forcing
  • telos — end, completion, the point of a thing
  • conatus — striving; the effort to persist in being
  • logos — account, reason, speech, proportion
  • li (principle 理) and li (ritual 禮) — two entirely distinct concepts that English renders identically
